newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares finish lower in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares finish lower in dull trade.

text.p: Share prices drifted lower on Tuesday at the Bombay bourses in sluggish trade with most participants staying on the sidelines, brokers said.
"It was a lacklustre market, very indecisive," said Ajit Sanghvi at broking firm Malini Ajit Sanghvi. "It was expected to go up, but it stayed down."
He said the absence of fresh news to bolster sentiment and a market holiday ahead kept market players away.
Stock markets across India are closed on Wednesday to mark the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, who led the country's fight for independence from Britain 50 years ago.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 12.64 points, or 0.39 percent, to a provisional 3,226.84.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index dropped 6.54 points, or 0.69 percent, to a provisional 937.46.
The 500-share CRISIL index eased 3.44 points, or 0.55 percent, to a provisional 622.76.
Heavy selling hurt SBI ahead of the bank's pricing of its issue of $400 million global depositary receipts on October 3.
SBI fell 6.75 rupees to 246.25 at the NSE, where trading was extended by half an hour to 1030 GMT to make up for lost time due to satellite problems, with over 18 million shares traded.
The share shed 3.0 rupees to 249.75 at the BSE. Petrochemicals share IPCL attracted short covering on news the depressed market for petrochemicals was showing signs of improvement, brokers said.
The stock gained 5.60 rupees to 118 at the NSE and 2.25 to 113.50 at the BSE.

ITC was pepped up by talk the tobacco conglomerate's British partner may raise its holdings, brokers said. The rumour could not be immediately confirmed. ITC firmed 7.90 rupees to 311.15 on the NSE and 2.0 to 302.25 at the BSE.
